applies_why: The judge text treats a single verse as admitting two readings and uses that as the ground for UNDERDETERMINED, which is the thing the rule governs.
quote: UNDERDETERMINED -- the passive egennēthē (was born) with feminine hēs (of whom) admits both the withheld-father and the birth-narration readings
rule_words: That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side. A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand. This is about one verse. It does not apply when the judge weighs two chains.
room: The phrase 'A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand.' I weighed whether 'admits both readings' makes a single verse open (forbidden) or states two senses standing (not UNDERDETERMINED).
why: The judge grounds UNDERDETERMINED on a single verse's admitting two readings, which K-S2 forbids.
